about: Mobile- und Servicerobotik 1 (MUS, 2nd semester) and 2 (MUS2, 3rd semester), FH Technikum Wien master's programme, after the slides of Wöber (2018, 2019, 2019a, 2021), the MUS 1 cheat sheet (Wöber 2020) and the convolutional networks slides of Thalhammer (2021). Pages are the PDF pages of each slide file, read in their text layer with pdftotext on 2 Nov 2026; equations shown only as images (the algorithm boxes after Thrun et al. 2006, the HSV and CNN examples) were read from page renderings. The course prints no worked numerical results except the network summary of the CNN slides (p. 10), so those counts are the only printed answers; the MUS Theoriefragen and the 2018 quizzes are questions in words. Every other answer was worked by hand from the course's equations and says so. tests/unit/labs-data.test.js recomputes every answer with the core and fails if they disagree.

practice.question: A door sensor sees a door in front of a door with p(s|d) = 0.6 and in front of a wall with p(s|¬d) = 0.3; before reading, door and wall are equally likely. It reports a door. How likely is it a door now?
practice.source: Worked by hand from Basics.pdf, p. 10 (the numbers are an example, not the course's)

practice.question: A corridor of 20 cells has doors in 4 of them. Starting with a flat belief, the same sensor (0.6 and 0.3) reports a door. What is the belief in one door cell now?
practice.source: Worked by hand from Basics.pdf, p. 21, line 4
practice.solution: Each door cell gets 0.6/20, each wall cell 0.3/20; the sum is (4·0.6 + 16·0.3)/20 = 7.2/20. Normalised, a door cell holds 0.6/7.2 = 0.0833.

labs.title: RANSAC: fit what most points agree on
